message: We've finished our draft recommendation to the council on whether to move its case-processing teams to a four-day week. It goes to an external reviewer next, Dr. Okafor, who hasn't seen any of the material or our draft. Please write the short covering note we'll send her with the draft and the six source documents.
response:
One thing to check before you send this: **R. Okafor is an author of two of the six sources.** She co-authored the Halden pilot (source 1) and the 24-month follow-up (source 5). If your reviewer is the same person, she would be reviewing a recommendation that rests partly on her own work. That includes the Halden findings the later sources criticised, and the follow-up that partly rehabilitates them. It may be a different Okafor, but it's worth confirming. If it is her, I'd either choose another reviewer or make sure the conflict is declared up front. The note below asks her to declare any connection, so it works either way.

I've also kept the note deliberately neutral. It doesn't summarise your conclusions or steer her toward particular issues, because an external review is most useful when she forms her own view of the sources first. I haven't seen your draft, so the bracketed parts are for you to fill in.

---

**Subject: External review – draft recommendation on a four-day week for case-processing teams**

Dear Dr Okafor,

Thank you for agreeing to review our draft recommendation to [council name] on whether to move its case-processing teams to a four-day week with pay maintained.

**Enclosed**

1. Our draft recommendation, [title, date]
2. The six documents it draws on:
   - Okafor, Brandt and Seo, *Reduced Working Time at Full Pay: Results from a Six-Month Multi-Organisation Pilot* (Halden Institute Working Paper 24-07)
   - Lindqvist, Mahony and Rao, *A Cluster-Randomised Trial of a 30-Hour Week in Municipal Administration: Nine-Month Results* (Varden County)
   - Varga and Holm, *Hours, Output and the Pilot Problem: A Re-examination of the Halden Reduced-Hours Pilot*
   - Achterberg, Iwu, Castell and Moreno, *Reduced Working Time and Productivity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis*
   - Lindqvist, Mahony, Rao and Okafor, *Two Years On: Follow-up of the Varden County Trial and a Subset of Halden Pilot Organisations*
   - *Does a Shorter Working Week Raise Productivity? A Synthesis of Five Sources* (evidence briefing prepared for the working group)

**What we are asking**

We would value your independent judgement on:

- whether the recommendation follows from the evidence, at the strength with which it is stated;
- whether any relevant evidence is missing, misread or given the wrong weight;
- how far the settings studied resemble the council's own case-processing work. [Add a sentence or two on the council's teams: size, type of casework, any statutory deadlines or public-facing duties.]
- anything else you think the council should know before deciding.

You may find it useful to read the sources before the draft. We have deliberately not summarised our conclusions here.

**Declaration of interests**

Two of the enclosed documents include an author named R. Okafor. If you are connected with any of the sources or their authors, please let us know before starting so we can record it.

**Timing**

We would be grateful for your comments by [date]. Please contact [name, role, contact details] with any questions.

With thanks,

[Name]
[Role, organisation]
